title: Also forgot to mention Nimene Sierra Wureh was a big standout for me ...
transcript: Taraji P Henson and Cedric the entertainer headline this revival from one of the greatest playwrights in the canon August Wilson's acclaimed 1984 play Joe Turner's Come and gone is back on Broadway, directed by Debbie Allen and this is particularly exciting for me because both times that I've read this play I appreciated it but I had a nagging suspicion that if I were to just see it live I would totally understand the hype around it and I was right! a lot of the power of the play is this sense of characters being kind of lost and adrift looking for something to root themselves down I understood that on the page but I found it more effective and easier to latch onto live because you're really placed as a fly on the wall in this boarding house watching people come and go it also has a lot more humor than I realized when reading it which you know just added some extra warmth and dimension and frankly a little extra entertainment value so yeah now I get the hype I feel more prepared to say with my full chest that this is one of the best plays from one of our best playwrights and I think this revival captures the core strengths of the play pretty well but not without some stumbling blocks a few quibbles here and there with the tone or the staging of certain moments but the biggest thing for me, unfortunately was how Debbie Allen and Joshua Boone interpreted the character of Harold Loomis and to be clear Joshua Boone is an excellent actor this is not remotely a question of his talent I just think they made some strong choices for this character that didn't really work for me and it's a reasonable interpretation of the character but I think they played it to an extremity that felt alienating to me and just kind of out of step with the rest of the production and the reason I'm focusing on this so much is that despite the character's mysterious aloofness he's kind of the closest thing we have to a protagonist not necessarily in terms of stage time but in terms of being like the crux of the plot the emotional and thematic centerpiece of the story so the performance has a big impact on the play but I was incredibly impressed with the rest of the cast Cedric the entertainer was a real standout he just did effortlessly had the audience in stitches every time he opened his mouth Taraji P Henson, totally solid, although this is kind of a small role for her but the best performance in the cast by far was Reuben Santiago-Hudson as Bynum and if you don't know this is a man who has an incredibly rich history with this body of work he is kind of *the* August Wilson guy in the modern day it's so obvious in this performance just the skill with which he commands the stage with this text and navigates the many shades of this character from the delightful humor to the captivating wisdom to his own human longings that help him guide others through theirs I really hope he wins the Tony for this his performance is pretty unmissable
classificationReason: Creator explicitly attended the revival (Taraji P. Henson, Cedric the Entertainer, directed by Debbie Allen) and shares a first-hand opinion: confirms the play's live power exceeded reading it, praises its humor and warmth, and notes the revival 'captures the core strengths... but not without some stumbling blocks.'
